Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app Agent (React page in a wxWebView, C++ host) and an MCP server so external AI tools can drive the open project through a stdio bridge. Branch jusprin-newui, HEAD around f073fdba96. A side session tested the MCP experience on 2026-10-21 and its report, mcp-experience-findings.md at the repo root (untracked), ranks "external-only edits are invisible in the app" as the top finding with the exact cause at App.tsx:415/421/581. Kenneth and I then brainstormed: he asked whether to create a chat on the first MCP call; I recommended against it because an MCP client has no chat concept, there is no stable moment to create one (a bridge process per client launch), and the active chat's change log already holds the edits like hand edits. He agreed, asked for the client-name refinement, and decided the "Set up the agent" offer becomes a small sticky button replacing the composer whenever a thread is shown without an agent, including the existing saved-history case. Conventions: logic goes in the page unless it touches Orca state; temporary docs stay untracked and are never committed or gitignored; never commit submodules; keep changes small and additive; no live-model runs that cost money without Kenneth's approval (a scripted MCP client costs nothing); attribute behaviour to OrcaSlicer only when upstream ships it.

Task:
Design and implement three related changes to the JusPrin Agent panel (the React page under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/ plus one small C++ addition). Read agent-docs/jusprin/README.md, then architecture.md ("Where logic goes: the page first" and "Agent WebView") and design-system.md ("Writing UI code"). Every colour, radius, font and size comes from the token file through the CSS variables; styles.test.ts fails on literals.

The problem. When no in-app agent is configured and an external MCP client (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop) edits the project, the person sees nothing. The edits are recorded: ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:947 files an MCP edit as EditActor::ExternalTool, ProjectStateDocument stores a ChangeEntry with external=true in the active conversation, work entries (a slice) are stored the same way, and the thread already draws them (ChangeRows.tsx labels the run "External tool"; WorkCard draws a slice). But App.tsx:415 computes onlyFileReports from state.messages alone, so a chat holding only change and work entries counts as empty, notConfigured becomes true, and body() returns AgentNotConfiguredPane (App.tsx:583) in place of the MessageList. The setup card's fallback line ("Preset fallback · No agent configured · using the selected preset") is also wrong once the preset has external edits. Kenneth has verified this with a real MCP client and decided the fix: do not create a chat per MCP client; the active chat's change log is the right place, as it is for hand edits.

Change 1: show the thread. A conversation counts as non-empty when it has change or work entries for the viewed conversation, not only messages. Then the normal chat header, setup card, MessageList (with the external change rows and work cards) render, and the setup card's fallback state yields to its edited state when changes exist (SetupCard.tsx receives `changes`; look at how "Edited by you" is derived and add the external case with wording like "Edited by an external tool"). Keep file-report notes behaving as today.

Change 2: name the client. McpProtocol.cpp:160 reads io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo (name, version) at initialize. Carry the client's display name through to the change entry so the row reads the client's name (for example "Claude Code") instead of "External tool", and the same on work entries a client starts if that is cheap. This is additive: a new optional string field on ChangeEntry (and the JSON the page receives via AgentHost.cpp:195 and ProjectStateDocument.cpp:1277/421), defaulting to the current "External tool" wording when absent. Check whether the runtime keeps clientInfo per connection (McpRuntime, McpServer) and the smallest way to pass it to the coordinator; do not add a session or chat concept for MCP. Prefer the official client name as sent, trimmed, capped at a sensible length.

Change 3: shrink the setup offer. Whenever the agent is unavailable and a thread is shown (external-only edits, and the existing case of saved history with no agent), replace the composer at the bottom of the chat panel with a compact sticky "Set up the agent" button that opens the existing setup flow (openSetup in App.tsx). The big AgentNotConfiguredPane stays only for a truly empty project with no history. Use the design system's button recipe and tokens; add a short one-line explanation only if the design system has a pattern for it. Design it first as a small sketch in words or a quick render; Kenneth's design source of truth is the Claude design artifacts (see design-system.md rule 5), not Figma, so do not touch Figma.

Tests: Vitest for the page (App.test.tsx has fixtures for the not-configured states and ChatPanel.preview.test.tsx / SetupCard tests for the card), styles.test.ts must stay green, and a Catch2 or agent_bridge test for the new change-entry field round-tripping through ProjectStateDocument. Prove the page test fails before the fix (inject the external-only state and assert the thread renders). Rebuild the web bundle the way the AgentUI README or CMake target does, and for the C++ field rebuild and run the relevant tests under build/arm64 (reuse the existing build; a full RelWithDebInfo rebuild is slow and another session may be building). If you can run the built app with an isolated --datadir and a scripted MCP client (the previous test session left mcpclient.py and the recipe in its report at mcp-experience-findings.md, untracked at the repo root), verify the panel end to end; otherwise say so.

Done looks like: the three changes on a branch cut from jusprin-newui, each as its own commit with a plain-English message, tests passing, and a short untracked note at the repo root saying what was verified live and what was not. Do not commit the note and do not add it to .gitignore. Do not commit submodule changes.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06

---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

# JusPrin MCP experience: findings (2026-10-21)

Working note, untracked. Do not commit.

## 1. Problem

JusPrin runs an MCP server inside the app so that external AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code) can drive the open project. External clients start a small stdio program, `jusprin-mcp` (the "bridge"), which forwards their calls to the app. The question was: when a real client uses this the way the setup screen tells a person to, does it work, can a model pick the right tool from the descriptions alone, do errors say what to call next, are results a sensible size, and does the app show the person what the external tool did?

Short answer: the core workflow works end to end, and most errors are good. The two biggest gaps are about the person rather than the protocol. First, a person who uses only an external tool sees nothing in the Agent panel about what that tool changed. Second, the error code `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary situations like "a slice is already running", while the server's own instructions tell the model that this code means "open JusPrin and a project". Everything else is smaller: inconsistent error codes, one counting bug, and one setup command that fails the second time.

## 2. What was tested and how

- **Build.** I used the existing `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app`, built at 04:16 today while HEAD was 05a044f707, which is the commit the gap review covered. Commits since then (f073fdba96) do not touch `Mcp/`, `ToolRegistry.cpp` or the workspace adapter. I copied the bundle to my scratchpad, gave the copy its own bundle id (`com.jusprin.mcp-experience-test`), and ad-hoc signed it, so the build could not overwrite it and screenshots could not bind to another JusPrin instance. A fresh RelWithDebInfo rebuild (919 steps) was too slow at load average 21 to 32. Another session was also building Release in the same build folder, so I stopped my build at step 253. The app binary used here is therefore from the reviewed commit, not today's HEAD.
- **Isolation.** The app ran as `OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch>/data <model>`, with `HOME=<scratch>/home`. Its config was `tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf` (stealth mode, version check pointed at a closed port, single instance off). The MCP server took port 47301. Kenneth's own data folder had no discovery file, so the ~75 `jusprin-mcp` processes belonging to other Claude sessions on this machine kept answering offline and never reached this instance. For the "agent configured" run, the config held a fake OpenAI key and the app ran with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`, so no model could be called or billed.
- **Client.** I wrote a scripted stdio MCP client (`mcpclient.py` in my scratchpad). It starts the bundled `jusprin-mcp --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` exactly as the Connect screen writes it into a client config, negotiates protocol `2025-06-18` as Claude Code does, and logs every exchange with its size and latency (388 calls). No paid model was used. The real Claude Code CLI was used only for `claude mcp add`, `mcp list` and `mcp get`, which make no model calls.
- **Covered:** initialize and version negotiation; `tools/list` with paging; offline behaviour; `workspace_inspect` (every section); `object_analyze`; `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `settings_preview_patch` and `settings_apply_patch`; `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`; `object_place` (rotate, position, autoOrient); `plate_layout` (quantity, arrange); `object_import_file`; `project_open` (new, STL, 3MF, the opened-before flow); `export_file`; `project_delete_items`; `presets_list`; `printer_setup_preview`; `printer_list`; `project_attachment_read`; `activity_cancel`.
- **Error paths covered:** a stale revision, a wrong session, unknown object, plate and setting ids, a bad enum value, a value out of range, blocked and withheld keys, wrong argument types, an extra field, an unknown tool, and a feature handle that has expired.
- **Lifecycle:** cancelling a slice, slicing while a slice is running, `preempt`, re-slicing an unchanged plate, a client cancelling its request, the client closing mid-call, two clients racing, calls made while a modal dialog is open, 40 objects, and an app quit and relaunch under a live client.
- **Screenshots** of the test app with and without an in-app agent configured.
- **Existing suites:** `JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<copy>/jusprin-mcp python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp` gave **18 tests, OK (1 skipped)**. `agent_bridge_tests "[mcp],[mcp_setup],[bridge]"` gave **All tests passed (894 assertions in 57 test cases)**, but that binary dates from 2026-10-20 19:30, before 05a044f707, which also changed `tests/agent`.

## 3. Results

### What works (verified)

- **Setup commands work the first time.** `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio jusprin -- <bridge> --discovery <data>/jusprin/mcp.json` printed "Added stdio MCP server jusprin". `claude mcp get jusprin` then printed `Status: ✔ Connected`.
- **Offline behaviour is clear.** With the app closed, `initialize` and `tools/list` still answer from the bridge's built-in catalog. A tool call returns `workspace_unavailable`: "Open JusPrin and a project, then try again. The bridge does not launch JusPrin."
- **Version negotiation.** A client asking for `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18` or `2025-11-25` gets that version. A client asking for `2024-11-05` is answered with `2025-06-18`.
- **Catalog.** There are 27 tools. The first page holds 25 (34,291 bytes on the wire) and the second page holds `view_render` and `workspace_inspect` (2,593 bytes). The descriptions are detailed and say which call comes next, for example "Preview first", "read from workspace_inspect's slicing section", and "Handles are valid until the project changes".
- **Settings workflow.** Preview of `{"wall_loops":4,"sparse_infill_density":"25%"}` returned before/after values and `valid: true`. Apply returned `applied: true` and moved the revision from 7 to 8. `settings_get` then showed `differsFromPreset: true`. Unknown keys come back with suggestions (`wall_loop` suggests `wall_loops`; `infil_density` suggests `sparse_infill_density`). A bad enum lists all 26 allowed values. Out of range gives `min`/`max`. Withheld keys (`print_host`) return a clear message saying the person changes it in the printer's connection settings.
- **Slicing.**
  - `slice_start` returns a handle immediately with a note that the client must poll. Slicing finished after about 30 s (111 s for three copies at load average 30).
  - `slice_report` (2.6 KB for all eight sections) gave time, grams, cost and Orca's own warning text.
  - `activity_cancel` stopped a running slice (`"cancelled": true`). A second `slice_start` with `preempt` replaced a running slice. Re-slicing an unchanged plate returned `alreadySliced: true` immediately. This means the hang recorded on 2026-10-15 (memory "manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe", trap 2) no longer happens.
- **Images.** `view_render` returned a 1024×768 PNG of 12,394 bytes as an MCP image block. It looked correct.
- **Stale handling.** Two clients previewed at the same revision and applied at the same time. The first applied. The second got `stale_workspace` with the expected and current revision, and nothing was changed twice. An expired face handle gives `feature_expired` with "Read the features again".
- **`project_open`.** The opened-before flow returns a clear question for the person ("Ask the person whether to continue that project or start a new one…"). Orca's own dialogs are answered and reported, for example "The 3MF is not supported by JusPrin, loading geometry data only."
- **Lifecycle.**
  - A `notifications/cancelled` sent before the call started meant the project was not opened.
  - When the client closed its input 0.3 s into `project_open`, the bridge exited in 0.01 s and the open still completed. This matches the documented "outcome unknown" behaviour.
  - With the Preferences dialog open, reads and a settings apply all completed and nothing hung.
  - The same bridge process followed the app through a quit and relaunch.

The cause is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, line 421: `notConfigured = unavailable && (… || onlyFileReports)`. Change-log entries are not messages, so a conversation that holds only external changes still counts as empty, and `body()` returns `AgentNotConfiguredPane` (line 581) in place of the thread. After a successful Connect, the "Connected" screen promises "Review its progress and results in this panel". For an external-only person, that promise is false.

**2. `workspace_unavailable` is used for ordinary refusals that the server instructions describe as "JusPrin is closed" (verified twice).** The server instructions say: "A workspace_unavailable error means you should open JusPrin and a project." `McpProtocol.cpp` `activity_result()` (line 261) maps every native `unavailable_operation` to `workspace_unavailable`. Two calls in this run came back with that code:
  - `slice_start` while a slice is running returned "A slice is already running. Wait for it, or ask again with preempt." (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2141`).
  - `export_file` of an unsliced plate returned "Slice the plate first; it has no current G-code" (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:331`).

The message text is right, but a model that follows the code and the instructions will tell the person to open JusPrin. These need their own codes, or the instructions need to stop treating the code as meaning "closed".

**3. The same mistake gets different error codes in different tools (verified).**

    - `slice_report` returns `invalid_arguments`, "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract.", with no details.
    - `slice_start` returns `invalid_id`, "No such plate".
    - `view_render` returns `stale_workspace`, "That plate is not in the open project", with `expectedRevision` equal to `currentRevision` (22 and 22), so the error claims the workspace changed when it did not. This comes from `WorkspaceError::StaleId` in `OrcaOutputs.cpp:151/328/338` and `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1556/1568/1573/2553/2604`, mapped in `McpProtocol.cpp` `activity_result()`.

  - A wrong argument type (`objectId: 59`) returns the contract message with no field name, while a missing field does name it ("Missing: include").

The summary then said `objectCount: 40`, the per-plate lists added up to 40, and the object appeared nowhere. The `objects` section still listed all 41, with `plateIds: []` for the moved one. `ToolResults.cpp` `workspace_inspection()` (around line 761) counts `plate.objects` instead of model objects. To a client reading the default view, the object looks deleted. The same sum would count an object twice if its copies sit on two plates; I did not test that case.

"Connect" for Claude Code fails if JusPrin was ever connected before (verified with the real CLI).** Running the same `claude mcp add --scope user … jusprin` a second time exits 1 with "MCP server jusprin already exists in user config". The Connect screen would then show the generic "The setup command failed." This blocks reconnecting after the app moves, after a reinstall, or after a data folder change, and the old entry stays pointed at the old path. With a moved app path, `claude mcp list` shows "✘ Failed to connect — ENOENT … posix_spawn". `codex mcp add` overwrites instead, and so does the JSON-file path for Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code. The correct next step, which the other `stale_workspace` message gives, is to read and preview again.

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.

The app's part:

- It decides which tools the model gets: the five printer tools and the four settings tools, the same list in every mode.
- It checks every tool call.
- It refuses a call that does not fit the conversation. Examples are adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one the conversation is about, and changing a setting on anything other than that printer.
- It refuses a turn that arrives with no instructions. The app has no prompt of its own to fall back on.
- It posts the opening line once per session.
- It posts the note for a tap only when the tap goes through, and limits the note to 2 KB.
- It still writes the notes for things only the app can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, the printer's model id is not on the list, or a save or an undo failed.

The project assistant works the same way. Its whole system prompt is written in `AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`, and `projectInstructions.test.ts` pins it to a fixture so that a change to it is always deliberate. The page sends it with `project_instructions` on every connection. The app keeps it in the project session's profile and sends it, unchanged, as the instructions of every project request; the provider's prompt cache depends on the text staying byte-identical. The app has no default text. A turn the app starts itself before the page has sent the prompt (the first message after a file opens, or Ask AI on a print issue, while the page is still loading) waits in the reply queue and starts when the prompt arrives. The prompt lived in C++ until 2026-10-14 so that the MCP server's instructions could share part of it; they stopped sharing it on 2026-10-10. The MCP server's own instructions (`Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp`) and the request that names a conversation stay in C++: MCP has no page, and the title request is the app's own.

Windows uses WebView2, macOS uses WKWebView, and Linux uses WebKitGTK. The way the page's files are packaged must work on all three. The prototype packed the whole page into a single local file, because WKWebView failed to load additional files referenced through `file:` URLs. Production keeps the single-file approach, and CMake now builds that file from the TypeScript/React sources.

MCP (Model Context Protocol, which lets external AI tools call the app) and wider agent autonomy are layers that come after this one. They must go through the same typed workspace interface. They must not change who owns the 3D view.

1. Show a compact strip of tool buttons in the upper-left corner of the Prepare canvas. The strip is a horizontal row like OrcaSlicer's own toolbar, but aligned to the left instead of centred. On every frame it asks the gizmo manager which tool is open. The open tool's values appear below the row in `Canvas/ToolValuePanel`, lined up with the button that opened the tool.
2. Activate the existing native gizmo.
3. Keep the existing pointer dragging, snapping, and selection behavior.

Semantic annotations are labels a person puts on part of a model to say what that part means, such as a face that must stay smooth. - Do not place WebView content over the native GL canvas.
- Do not keep a second copy of the project model or of the undo stack in JavaScript.

- Do not try to match every stock OrcaSlicer feature when the product definition does not require it.

1. Write the canonical product documents, and set up the design tokens and the curated assets.
2. Bring the workspace interface up to production quality: the interface itself, commands that go through OrcaSlicer's own code, change observation, and tests against the real adapter.

4. Build the production shell without a compact object/plate pane.

# Composer

The message box at the bottom of the Agent pane, following common AI chat apps: staged files, a text area that grows with the message, and a toolbar to attach, choose the model and thinking level, and send.

- You supply `value`, `onChange`, `onSend`, `onAttach(type)` and optionally `state` (`idle`, `streaming` or `unavailable`), `mode` (`regular` or `photo`), `attachments` (the props of each staged `ChatAttachment`), `models` with `model` and `onModelChange`, `thinkingLevels` with `thinking` and `onThinkingChange`, `onStop` and `placeholder`.
- One box with `space-8` padding, `space-4` between its parts, `radius-medium` corners and a 1px `border-subtle` stroke, on `surface-canvas`. Staged files sit inside it above the text, `space-4` apart.
- The text area starts one line high in `body-small` and grows a line at a time up to `component-composer-maxLines` (8) lines, then the text scrolls inside it. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. The placeholder is `text-tertiary`.
- The toolbar: on the left a `ButtonIcon` with `plus`, then the model picker, then the thinking picker; on the right a compact `ButtonPrimary` labelled Send. A picker is `label` text and a `chevron-down`, `space-4` by `space-8` padding, `radius-small`; it fills with `surface-selected` while its menu is open.
- + opens a `MenuPopover` above it with four `MenuRow`s: Photo or image, 3D model (STL, 3MF, STEP), G-code, Document (PDF). Each opens the system file picker filtered to that type.
- When the pane is too narrow for both full labels beside + and Send, the thinking picker drops "Thinking:" and shows the level alone ("Medium"); if that still does not fit, the model name is cut with "…". + and Send keep their size.
- A model menu with more than 12 models starts with a `FieldSearch` ("Search models") above the provider groups, and opens with the cursor in it and the highlight on the chat's current model. Typing filters by model or provider name, ignoring case; providers with no match drop out, the first match is highlighted (Enter picks it, Up and Down move), and with no match the list reads "No models match “…”." Escape clears the search, a second Escape closes the menu. The list scrolls under the field. With 12 models or fewer there is no field. See the canvas board "model-menu-search · proposal".
- The model menu lists the models of every connected provider, each group under a `MenuSectionTitle` with the provider's name; with one provider the heading is left out. The thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model supports, and the thinking picker is left out for a model without levels. Switching models keeps the level if the new model has it, otherwise it falls back to that model's default. Both choices apply to the current chat only.
- Send is disabled until there is text or a file; a file alone can be sent. While the Agent is replying the placeholder reads "Agent is responding…", Send becomes a Stop `ButtonSecondary`, and + and the pickers are disabled.
- Unavailable is different from empty: the box turns `surface-subtle`, the placeholder reads "Chat is unavailable" in `action-disabled-text`, and everything but the text is disabled.
- Photo mode (the printer chat, where only a photo can be attached) shows a "Photo" `ButtonLink` instead of + and has no pickers.
- Keyboard focus in the text draws a 2px `border-focus` stroke around the whole box.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
